findings.title: [P1] Retain and unregister the message handler on unmount
findings.body: `unmount()` no longer detaches the `"message"` listener, and the handler reference is destroyed, making the subscription permanent. The diff removes `this.socket?.off("message", this.onMessage)` and registers an inline anonymous callback instead (`socket.on("message", message => this.render(message))`), storing no reference that `off()` could accept. Trigger: any socket that outlives the view — `mount(sock)` → `unmount()` → sock emits a message — still invokes `this.render(message)` on the unmounted view, producing stale rendering after teardown/navigation/logout. The closure also keeps the `SocketView` reachable from the socket (memory retention), and repeated mount/unmount cycles accumulate listeners and duplicate renders without bound. Fix: keep a stored handler (e.g. `this.onMessage = message => this.render(message)`) and restore the `off()` call in `unmount()`.
